newsitem.title: CHINA: HK govt expects to achieve housing target in 2001.
newsitem.headline: HK govt expects to achieve housing target in 2001.

text.p: Hong Kong Secretary for Housing Dominic Wong said on Friday that the government could achieve its annual housing supply target of 85,000 units by 2001.
"By the year 2001, we would be able to reach the average level of 85,000 flats. Beyond that we should be able to build no less than 85,000," he told Reuters in an interview.

"For this year the production levels will rise. Next year it will rise further. This year we expect a supply of 22,000 flats from the private sector. Next year, our present estimate according to information on hand is about 36,000 private flats."
Wong said that for 1999, a total of 40,000 private flats could be achieved.
Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa said in his inaugural speech on July 1 that the government planned to increase overall housing supply to a target of not less than 85,000 flats per year.

Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said about 79,000 new private and public flats would be released each year for the next three years and thereafter about 104,000 new flats would be released each year until 2004/05.
